models.name: Byrdland
models.note: The 1959 Sunburst count conflicts between published records: 40 versus 46. An exact count for that cell is withheld. These are short-scale thinline archtops.

models.name: EB-3
models.note: Through 1970 the source combines finishes and may include long-scale EB-3L examples. From 1971 the long-scale variant has its own rows.

models.name: EB-6
models.note: The source spans the hollowbody-to-solidbody transition in 1962; body style cannot be inferred solely from a year total.

models.name: ES-150 (Postwar Deep Body)
models.note: Only the postwar deep-body ES-150 series is included here. The later ES-150DC is a different model.

models.name: ES-355TD (Mono)
models.note: This is the mono version. The source does not separate its finishes. Do not label its whole total Cherry.

models.name: ES-355TDSV (Stereo)
models.note: This is the stereo/Varitone version. Its shipments are separate from mono ES-355TD shipments, and the source does not break out finishes.

models.name: Firebird I
models.note: The 1965 totals span the reverse-to-non-reverse transition. This source does not separate body styles or custom colors.

models.name: Firebird III
models.note: The 1965 totals span the reverse-to-non-reverse transition. This source does not separate body styles or custom colors.

models.note: The 1965 totals span the reverse-to-non-reverse transition. This source does not separate body styles or custom colors.

models.name: Firebird XII
models.note: The 1965 totals span the reverse-to-non-reverse transition. This source does not separate body styles or custom colors.

models.name: J-200
models.note: The references disagree on 1950 Natural (37 versus 39) and 1959 Sunburst (97 versus 91). Those cells are shown as disputed.

models.name: L-7CE (McCarty, One Pickup)
models.note: McCarty electric-pickguard category. C identifies cutaway; D identifies two pickups. Keep these electric variants distinct from acoustic L-7 and L-7C shipments.

models.name: L-7CED (McCarty, Two Pickups)
models.note: McCarty electric-pickguard category. C identifies cutaway; D identifies two pickups. Keep these electric variants distinct from acoustic L-7 and L-7C shipments.

models.name: L-7E (McCarty, One Pickup)
models.note: McCarty electric-pickguard category. C identifies cutaway; D identifies two pickups. Keep these electric variants distinct from acoustic L-7 and L-7C shipments.

models.name: L-7ED (McCarty, Two Pickups)
models.note: McCarty electric-pickguard category. C identifies cutaway; D identifies two pickups. Keep these electric variants distinct from acoustic L-7 and L-7C shipments.

models.name: L-48 / L-50
models.note: No checked annual shipment series is included here.

models.name: Les Paul 55
models.note: The 1976 to 1979 sequence 2, 331, 293, 224 belongs to the Les Paul 55. The Pro Deluxe is a different model.

models.name: Les Paul Artisan
models.note: The earlier annual figures have no independently checked table citation in this edition.

models.name: Les Paul Bass / Triumph
models.note: The source continued the Les Paul Bass label into the Triumph period. Earlier totals cannot be split reliably into the two designs. Separate Triumph finish rows begin in 1975.

models.name: Les Paul Deluxe
models.note: Finish, left-handed and full-size-humbucker rows remain separate. The 1976 Goldtop standard-listing figure is 34; the sum of all listed 1976 categories is 172. Later records should not be treated as a complete count from every Gibson factory.

models.name: Les Paul Junior (Original Slab Body)
models.note: The 1958 figure combines single-cutaway and double-cutaway Juniors. TV Models and 3/4-scale Juniors are separate categories. The checked series places 2,408 in 1958, 4,364 in 1959 and 2,513 in 1960.

models.name: Les Paul Model / Standard (1952 To 1960)
models.note: These are model-branch shipment totals. The 1958 count of 434 combines Goldtops and Sunbursts. Pickup, bridge and finish changes within a year cannot be separated from this series.

models.name: Les Paul Pro Deluxe
models.note: No checked annual shipment series is available in this edition. The previously used sequence belongs to the Les Paul 55.

models.name: Les Paul Special (Original Slab Body)
models.note: This series reports model totals, including finish and body changes within a year. It does not supply a dependable Cherry/TV or single/double-cutaway split.

models.name: Les Paul Standard (1968 To 1979)
models.note: The earlier page mixed differently defined reissue and Standard entries. Annual figures are withheld until each original category can be checked.

models.name: Les Paul TV Model
models.note: TV Model is a separate ledger category. Published transcriptions differ on the 1955 count; that year is withheld from exact totals pending a ledger check.

models.name: LG-0
models.note: The source leaves 1970 blank. The gap is not treated as zero shipments.

models.name: LG-1 / LG-2 / LG-3 / B-25
models.note: These related names cover distinct models and transitions. No complete checked annual series is included here.

models.name: Moderne
models.note: No verified 1958 or 1959 shipment count is included. The 19 and 3 figures refer to the Explorer.

models.name: SG / Les Paul Junior
models.note: The SG-shaped Junior first appears in this series in 1961. White examples can exist even where this source gives no finish breakdown.

models.name: SG TV (Ledger Category)
models.note: The reference itself is uncertain whether this category includes both Juniors and Specials. Keep it separate from either named model; do not add it to an SG family total.
